name: Mediterranean Acacia-Argania dry woodlands and succulent thickets
about: The low, dry eastern islands, Lanzarote and Fuerteventura, under a dusty trade-wind sky: black lava fields and red and black cinder cones at Timanfaya, vines in walled pits of black ash at La Geria, the sheer Risco de Famara over a white-surf beach, wide ochre plains and worn brown domes round Betancuria with aulaga, tabaiba and prickly pear, the pale dunes of Corralejo, the wild beach of Cofete under the Jandía ridge, white cubic villages with green or brown woodwork, palms by the farms and goats everywhere. No split: both islands share one dry haze, one weather and one grade; black young lava and ash lie on both islands (Timanfaya, La Geria; Malpaís Grande, Bayuyo) as ochre old basalt does (Los Ajaches, Famara; Betancuria, Jandía), so the ground colour follows the rock's age in IGME rock colour, Sentinel-2 colour and the NDVI ramps, not the island; the bare lava and sand follow the barren rule, the Famara and Jandía cliffs follow WorldCover and the cliffs rule, palms and tamarisks follow the tree elevation bands, and the whole region is one subdivision (es-cn) for its houses. The trade-wind cloud cap on the Risco de Famara and the Jandía ridge is a height question for the weather, not an area: try mistTop and the cloud base first, then a height rule. La Graciosa, the other Chinijo islets and Lobos lie just outside the ecoregion outline.
